transcript:
Header:
Date: 2026-03-04
Start: 15:30 PT
Duration: ~42 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Arjun Patel (Redwood SE), Liam O'Connor (SilverArch Head of Eng), Priya Mehta (ML Lead), Noah Reyes (CTO)

Summary:
Short discovery focused on trying Redwood's PLG quickstart. Customer is primarily exploring hosted for fast POC but wants clarity on Dedicated/Private for production. Key asks: how fast to first token, free credits, sample throughput/latency numbers, security compliance (SOC2 + KMS), and an eval plan.

Topics covered:
- Redwood quickstart flow (signup, API keys, free credits)
- Time-to-first-token and minimal integration steps
- Dedicated vs Hosted vs Private tradeoffs for cost and compliance
- Security: SOC2, SSO/SAML, KMS, audit logs, data retention
- Benchmarks and pilot scope

Transcript body:
[00:00] Maya Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick intros from our side, I'm Maya, I'm the AE, and Arjun is our solutions engineer.
[00:08] Arjun Patel: Hi all. We'll mostly walk through the quickstart and then dig into any infra or security q's.
[00:14] Liam O'Connor: Thanks, Maya. Quick context - we're SilverArch, building an internal dev-assist product. We're evaluating hosted first for speed, but we have to consider dedicated for cost predictability and private for data residency.
[00:30] Maya Chen: Totally makes sense. Today we'll show the PLG path - sign up, redeem credits, hit the API, and then discuss how Dedicated/Private map to your requirements.
[00:42] Priya Mehta: Two quick ones up front - how fast can we get first token after signup, and do the free credits cover a meaningful smoke test?
[00:50] Arjun Patel: Typical time-to-first-token is under 10 minutes if you follow the quickstart. That includes creating an API key, running a curl sample and getting a streaming response. Free credits are sized for a small POC - ~50k tokens worth which usually covers a couple of smoke tests and a demo.
[01:10] Noah Reyes: 50k tokens - can you translate into QPS or latency? We care about tail latency more than average.
[01:18] Arjun Patel: Sure - for our hosted RL models the p50 latency for short prompts is ~60-120ms per token, p95 varies by model and sequence length. We can share model profiles. For tail, we recommend a small warmup and prefix caching. Note: in conversation I might say 'KV cash' sometimes - I mean KV cache.
[01:40] Liam O'Connor: Haha, KV cash - got it. Regarding Dedicated: is that reserved GPUs with an SLA?
[01:46] Maya Chen: Yes, Dedicated is reserved capacity, predictable throughput and optional burst. It comes with an SLA and better isolation. Private gives you VPC control and on-prem as an option for regulated workloads.
[02:00] Priya Mehta: On security - we're SOC2 and ISO on our roadmap. We need to know about audit logs, KMS/HSM integrations, SSO - SAML or OIDC?
[02:10] Arjun Patel: We support SAML and OIDC for SSO and RBAC at the route and team level. For encryption we integrate with customer KMS and can support bring-your-own-key patterns. Audit logs are available via the console and can be exported to your SIEM. We have SOC2 reports that we can share under an NDA.
[02:28] Noah Reyes: What's the friction for trying hosted quickstart given our security posture? We can't share PII to third parties.
[02:34] Maya Chen: For the quickstart you can use synthetic or anonymized data. If you need to test with sensitive data we can discuss a Dedicated pilot or Private control plane. Many customers do a hosted eval with redacted data to validate integration and then switch to Dedicated/Private for production.
[02:52] Liam O'Connor: Makes sense. On costs - do you have ballpark unit economics? We're trying to compare to running our own model infra.
[03:00] Arjun Patel: We typically provide per-token pricing for hosted and per-GPU/month for Dedicated. The Optimize toolkit can recommend batching/quant profiles to reduce unit cost. If you share your expected QPS/prompt lengths we can run a cost simulation in the benchmark spreadsheet.
[03:18] Priya Mehta: We'll share a sample prompt set and expected QPS. We're small right now - maybe 10-20 reqs/sec peak for initial rollout.
[03:26] Maya Chen: Perfect. That fits within our PLG-to-dedicated progression.
[03:32] Liam O'Connor: A couple of technical follow-ups - do you provide client SDKs with streaming support? And what languages?
[03:38] Arjun Patel: Yes, SDKs for Python, Node and Go; streaming, function calling and structured output all supported. We also have a simple REST curl sample that demonstrates a streaming chunked response for time-to-first-token checks.
[03:52] Noah Reyes: If we do a quick hosted eval, what's the recommended integration path? We have a small backend service that calls the API; we want minimal to no infra changes.
[03:59] Maya Chen: Minimal - create an API key in the console, integrate using one of the SDKs or curl, and run smoke tests. We'll provide sample code and a Postman collection. Arjun will share the exact curl to measure time-to-first-token.
[04:12] Priya Mehta: Great. Can you also share model latency profiles? We need p50/p95 numbers and token cost so we can calculate SLA needs.
[04:19] Arjun Patel: Yes - I'll attach our model performance spreadsheet. Note that model names in the docs may be slightly different from what you see - transcription can show model names weirdly, e.g., 'red wood' vs Redwood, or 'Mistral labs' spelled differently in a transcript.
[04:36] Liam O'Connor: (laughs) noted. On the legal side, procurement will want standard DPA/TOU and info on data residency. Is that part of the enterprise pack?
[04:44] Maya Chen: We have compliance add-ons and enterprise contracts that include data residency controls and extended SLA. I'll send the security docs and a standard DPA.
[04:52] Noah Reyes: For Dedicated, do you allow customer-managed networking? We need the option to put the inferencing nodes inside our VPC for east-west data flow reasons.
[04:59] Arjun Patel: Dedicated supports VPC peering and private networking; Private deployments give you a customer-managed control plane when needed. For truly air-gapped environments we offer an on-prem package.
[05:12] Priya Mehta: Any caveats around webhook callbacks or streaming? We need to ensure payloads stay internal.
[05:18] Arjun Patel: Webhooks can be configured to point to your endpoints. For hosted we recommend TLS+mutual TLS for sensitive callbacks, or you can put a dedicated proxy inside your VPC for extra control.
[05:28] Liam O'Connor: What does a typical pilot look like? Timeframe and success criteria?
[05:33] Maya Chen: Usually a 2-4 week pilot: week 1 quickstart + smoke tests, week 2 run benchmarks and a small integration, weeks 3-4 iterate on performance and cost tuning. Success criteria: passing latency SLOs for p95, acceptable cost per query, and no blocking security gaps.
[05:50] Priya Mehta: OK. We'll aim to provide prompt set and expected QPS by Monday.
[05:54] Noah Reyes: Can you confirm free credits cover the smoke tests you mentioned?
[05:58] Arjun Patel: Yes - the initial credit bundle covers ~50k tokens, usually enough for the smoke scenarios. If you need more we can top up depending on engagement.
[06:08] Liam O'Connor: Anything else we should know before we sign up?
[06:11] Maya Chen: Make sure you have a non-sensitive sample and a contact for procurement/security; we'll route the SOC2 NDA and security packet. Arjun will send the curl for TTFT.
[06:21] Priya Mehta: Quick nit - do you have any sample configs for batching or quantization suggestions for small models?
[06:26] Arjun Patel: Yep, Optimize provides recommendations; for initial pilots we often suggest moderate batching and int8 quant to reduce cost while preserving quality. We'll share our recommendation doc.
[06:36] Liam O'Connor: Sounds good. Let's schedule a technical demo next week to run the benchmark together.
[06:40] Maya Chen: I'll send calendar invites for the week of 3/9.
[06:44] Noah Reyes: Perfect. Thanks everyone.
[06:46] Maya Chen: Thanks all - we'll follow up with the quickstart steps and the links.

Notes about transcription quality: Some words were auto-transcribed incorrectly (e.g., 'KV cash' for KV cache, 'red wood' for Redwood). Speaker labels are mostly accurate but there were brief overlaps.
